clarifyingQuestions: Should low traffic hold even if metrics look bad?
Should a missing metric hold or roll back?
followUpGuide: Confidence intervals quantify sampling uncertainty after the traffic gate. Define the confidence level, minimum effect, and rule for an interval crossing the promotion boundary. Repeated polling also needs a sequential-testing policy; apply that policy and promotion rule together when deciding whether to promote.
Segment checks prevent an aggregate win from hiding failures for one tenant or device class.
Rollback cooldown avoids repeated promotion attempts while the same issue is active.
complexityAnalysis: - Fixed-field canary judge: compare a constant handful of dict fields. Time: O(1). Space: O(1).
- Multi-slice judge follow-up: aggregate metrics by route, model, or cohort before gating. Time: O(n). Space: O(s), where n is events and s is slice count.

- Streaming judge follow-up: counters can update in O(1); exact rolling quantiles need an ordered structure supporting insertion and expiration, typically O(log W) per event. Time: depends on the chosen quantile structure. Space: O(s * W) for s slices retaining W events each; bounded approximate sketches have different bounds.
solutionGuide: Gate low traffic first. After that, collect rollback reasons in deterministic order.
